criteria.evidence: Both expected directional sections are present and substantive: 'Directional intent' (two paragraphs) and 'Agent intent (ICE)' with Goal, Limit and Fails-if lines.

"It matters because each customer who comes back and buys is a sale the owner keeps instead of losing." and "respecting their consent here is what keeps a won-back sale from costing the shop that customer's trust."
Directional intent is a prose paragraph, as the directional guidance asks; the ICE section is discrete lines: "- Goal: ...", "- Limit: ...", "- Fails if: ...". No user-story phrasing.

Domain gives one line: "lets an owner remind the customer behind an abandoned cart to come back and finish the order, in one click." The capability adds what it owns: "deciding which customer is reminded, when, and with what message", the boundary with notifications, and its own ICE.

"letting a shop owner act on an abandoned cart straight away, by reminding the customer who left it" (what); "a sale the owner keeps instead of losing" (why); "The delivery channel itself... and the shared rules about who may be contacted and how often come from the notifications side" (edges).
